You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where contributing benefits the group more than the individual—each token kept is worth 1 to me, but contributed it only returns 0.3 to me despite generating 1.2 total. Pure self-interest says defect, but maximizing collective welfare favors contributing; I'm weighing whether to fully cooperate or find a middle ground.

Since I can't observe individual contributions across the 10 rounds, only group totals, I can't condition my strategy on others' specific behavior. I'll start with a fair opening contribution of 10 to signal cooperation without being fully exploited.
